clue.text: 10 observes 10 concealing drug

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hold it hidden inside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: the second 10 is SAINT, and Simon is one of the apostles honoured as a saint
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: One holy man watches another who is hiding narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SAINT, a cross-reference used throughout this puzzle. SIMON holding E gives SIMEON; 'observes' fits because Simeon is the saint who saw the infant Jesus in the Temple.
explanation.definitionFit: Simeon is venerated as a saint, the devout old man of Luke's gospel who blessed the child Jesus.

clue.text: 10 to tread on pecker

parts.note: a tread is a step, as on a staircase
a hen is a bird that pecks; 'on' places it after the first piece

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to a saint to stamp on a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SAINT. In a down clue 'on' means written after, so the pecker follows the tread.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen was the first Christian martyr and is honoured as a saint by the church.

clue.text: Substance of sound strength?

indicators.note: sound tells us the next word is to be heard rather than spelt as it stands

parts.note: mettle is strength of character, pronounced the same as the material

explanation.surface: A question asking what solid strength is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it is the signal that mettle and its twin are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron, copper or tin is a metal, a kind of material or physical stuff.

clue.text: Find one's way from one side of London, always following the short way

parts.note: the Orient is the east, and Leyton Orient is the football club of east London

indicators.note: writing a word the short way means contracting it, so a letter is dropped from the middle

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: Directions across London that keep taking the shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: The short way of writing ever is the poetic e'er, which loses its V. 'Following' puts it after the east.
explanation.definitionFit: To orienteer is to navigate across country with map and compass, a sport of route-finding.

clue.text: 10 Christopher heading for Africa instead of US

indicators.note: instead of says one thing takes the place of another within a word

parts.note: Christopher Columbus, the explorer
the letters US, removed from the surname

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Africa

explanation.surface: An explorer turning towards Africa rather than America.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SAINT. 'US' looks like America, fitting Columbus, but it is simply the two letters at the end of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Columba was the Irish monk who founded the abbey on Iona and is honoured as a saint.

clue.text: 10 is balmy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 10 across is SAINT, here an early pope canonised

explanation.walkthrough: As throughout this puzzle, 10 stands for SAINT, so the first definition is the name of a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild and pleasant, a synonym of balmy; Clement is also a saint's name.

clue.text: Composer's record listened to

indicators.note: something listened to is heard, so its pronunciation counts, not its spelling

parts.note: a list is a record of items, pronounced like the Hungarian's surname

explanation.surface: A composer's recording being played to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' suggests a disc to listen to; it is a written list.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian pianist and composer of the Hungarian Rhapsodies.

clue.text: Something put on paper by me, a fascist leader and politician (written inside)

definitions.text: Something put on paper by me, a fascist leader

indicators.note: written inside means set down within the other letters, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: taken as written
to ink is to put on paper
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the first letter of fascist
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A dictator describing his own book, with a politician scribbling in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole cryptic description of Hitler's book, and its words are reused by the wordplay, a setter's double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Mein Kampf is the book Hitler wrote, setting out his fascist programme, so it is literally his writing.

clue.text: 10 might be sinner if married at last?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a holy man who could turn bad
setter's reading: the name belongs to a hermit saint, and also to the Roman whose marriage and love affair made him a famous sinner

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SAINT. St Antony of Egypt was the desert hermit; Mark Antony married Octavia but strayed with Cleopatra, the sinner of the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: One name serves a desert saint and Mark Antony, the Roman general whose adultery with Cleopatra made him a sinner.

clue.text: Compensation will be given for gentle slap you received

indicators.note: what is received is taken in, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: a pat is a light tap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A promise of damages for a mild slap someone suffered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Received' looks like the victim taking the slap; it is the slap that takes in the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: A payout is a sum of money handed over, such as damages or an insurance settlement.

clue.text: Manage to get out of cart — it rolled into the river

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: something rolled tumbles over, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cart has tipped into a river and someone must free it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manage to get out of' looks like part of the story, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate is to free or disentangle, getting oneself or something out of a difficulty.

clue.text: He certainly isn't a crook …

parts.note: a crook is a villain or swindler; the man described is the opposite, a holy and virtuous person

explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots carry the sense on to the next clue; read alone, this one describes a person of perfect virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: A canonised holy person is the very model of goodness, nothing like a swindler or villain.

clue.text: … though he offered money 25% off to her

indicators.note: 25% off removes one of the four letters, the final quarter

parts.note: to have offered money as a loan is to have lent it

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a man offered her money at a quarter off.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the clue before: Paris won Helen of Troy. LENT loses its last quarter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to the woman the previous clue is about.

clue.text: Using wood around the green, was beaten for speed

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes on either side of the other

parts.note: oaken means made of oak
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: A golfer with a wooden club near the green lost on pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' and 'green' suggest golf; vert is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overtaken means another vehicle or runner passed you, so you were outpaced.

clue.text: 10 and religious text going round the globe with its owner?

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: NT is the New Testament
an orb is a globe, part of the royal regalia
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen who carries the royal orb

explanation.surface: A saint and a holy book circling the world and its master.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SAINT. The orb is the jewelled globe of the coronation regalia, held by the monarch, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Norbert of Xanten founded the Premonstratensian order and was canonised as a saint.

clue.text: Dress tried on in performance

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or set in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A costume being fitted during a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like a costume noun; it is a verb meaning arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is an interpretation or rendering of a song or piece, a performance of it.

clue.text: Vehicle negotiating bend, given a shock

indicators.note: a vehicle negotiating a curve has it within its path, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle
a U-bend, shaped like the letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A passenger jolted as a tram takes a sharp corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is emotional or physical shock, the lasting harm left by a distressing experience.

clue.text: 10 takes a vote on perfect inversion

parts.note: taken as written
a poll is a vote
taken as written

indicators.note: an inversion turns something upside down, which in a down clue means reading it backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written as A and the letter I

explanation.surface: A saint holds a ballot on whether to perfect a reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SAINT. A1, first class, is read as AI and turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollonia of Alexandria was a virgin martyr and is the patron saint of dentists.

clue.text: 10 asks for doctor to come again

indicators.note: asking for something means wanting it brought in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: anew means again
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A saint requests that the doctor call back.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SAINT; the doctor sits inside the word for again.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew, the fisherman apostle, is the patron saint of Scotland, whose cross is on its flag.

clue.text: Offered grouse, like a bird retaining height

indicators.note: retaining means keeping hold of, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: birds have wings
h is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: Someone served game bird, like a high-flying bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like the game bird, which fits 'bird', but it is a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to grumble, so offering a grouse is complaining, and whinged means complained peevishly.

clue.text: Authoress involved in lanolin

parts.note: Virginia Woolf, the novelist
at means in, as in at home

explanation.surface: A woman writer mixed up in hand cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved in' looks like a container signal; it is a link and 'in' gives AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the greasy substance from sheep's fleece, also called wool fat or wool grease.

clue.text: Composer's loveless charioteer

indicators.note: loveless means without love, which in crosswords is zero, the letter that looks like it, so it is removed

parts.note: a wagoner drives a wagon or chariot

explanation.surface: A composer's charioteer who has no sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is nil in tennis, hence the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was the German composer of the Ring cycle of operas.

clue.text: Mosaic depicting gods of Greece and Egypt upside-down

definitions.note: a tessera is a piece of a mosaic, so the noun stands loosely for the whole

indicators.note: turned upside-down in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
Set is the Egyptian god of chaos

explanation.surface: A mosaic showing ancient deities, hung the wrong way up.
explanation.walkthrough: One god of each nation, the pair then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles or cubes of stone or glass from which mosaics are built.

clue.text: Racketeer is a legend on the way up

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a saga is a legend or epic tale

explanation.surface: A gangster becoming a legend as his career rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racketeer' suggests a gangster; here it is one who wields a tennis racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi was the American champion tennis player, a playful sense of someone with a racket.

clue.text: Briefly making out, horse comes home lame on the inside

indicators.note: being on the inside means sitting within, so one piece is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
a lame horse limps in at the finish

explanation.surface: A racehorse finishing the race with a limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' belongs to the definition: a glimpse is a short look.
explanation.definitionFit: Glimpsing is catching sight of something only for a moment, seeing it fleetingly.

clue.text: 10 to dwindle

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to fade away little by little, as in the phrasal verb with 'out'

explanation.walkthrough: 10 stands for SAINT throughout this puzzle; the verb sense is usually heard in the phrase 'peter out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To peter is to diminish gradually, the verb behind 'peter out', and Peter is also the apostle and saint.

clue.text: 10 Joe, who was rarely flawed, we hear

definitions.text: Joe, who was rarely flawed, we hear
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Joe the heavyweight boxing champion, rarely knocked down; 'flawed' is said like 'floored'

explanation.walkthrough: The pun is inside the clue: 'flawed, we hear' is 'floored', pointing to the boxer Joe Louis, who was seldom knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis is the surname of the boxer Joe and the name of the French king canonised as St Louis.

clue.text: Like the Trout Quintet at a rock concert, perhaps, piano tuna may be fishy?

definitions.text: Like the Trout Quintet at a rock concert, perhaps

indicators.note: something fishy is suspect and not as it should be, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: p is the musical notation for piano, softly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Schubert's Trout Quintet would be out of place at a rock gig, with fish and piano puns.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trout Quintet is a Schubert chamber piece with piano; the fishy theme runs from trout to tuna.
explanation.definitionFit: Unapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, as classical chamber music would be at a rock show.

clue.text: A satirist must be quick

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Jonathan ..., author of Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: A rule that satire needs a fast wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift was the great Irish satirist, and swift is an everyday adjective for fast.

clue.text: Censor author about to produce something fruity

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Graham Greene, the novelist
to gag is to silence or censor

explanation.surface: A censor bearing down on a writer for racy material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' hints at risqué writing, but the answer is literally a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a sweet green variety of plum, so it is indeed something fruity.

clue.text: Italian man heading off to bed — non-starter, as was given the cold shoulder

indicators.note: with its heading off a word loses its first letter

parts.note: signor is the Italian for Mr

indicators.note: a non-starter has no start, so the first letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian off to bed, snubbed and going nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the cold shoulder is to snub them, deliberately paying them no attention.

clue.text: 10 suffering 15 (turn to hospital)

indicators.note: suffering means being in a bad way, so the letters are knocked out of order
turning one letter to another means swapping it for that letter

parts.note: 15 across is TRAUMA
a U-turn, so turn gives the letter U
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A saint is suffering from some shock, so is taken to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 stands for SAINT and 15 for the answer to 15 across; the bracket tells you to change one letter of 15 before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: St Martha, sister of Mary and Lazarus, is a saint of the New Testament.
